newsitem.title: USA: Internet market to top $100 billion in 2000, researcher says.
newsitem.headline: Internet market to top $100 billion in 2000, researcher says.

text.p: Sales of goods and services used to build and access the Internet will top $100 billion by the year 2000, nearly triple the $34.97 billion in sales of 1996, Zona Research, a firm specialising in tracking the Internet and electronic commerce, said Monday.

Zona's report characterised the Internet market as goods and services used to build and service Internet infrastructure. It does not include other types of products sold over the worldwide computer network.

Communications, including Internet-related equipment such as routers and modems, along with services by providers of Internet access and consultants, accounted for half of all Internet-related sales in 1996, or a total of $20.36 billion, Zona said.

It predicted Internet communications sector sales will jump to $62.8 billion in 2000, when the total market for building the Internet and related internal corporate intranet networks should reach nearly $107 billion.

"We've always known that the bandwith area is really where the bucks were," said Zona President Stephen Auditore. He predicted that communications would remain the largest segment for Intranet infrastructure despite the tendency of media and investor attention to focus on the "browser wars" between Microsoft Corp. and Netscape Communications Corp.
The containment sector -- Internet servers, server software, site hosting and services and maintenance -- was the second-largest segment in 1996, with sales of $7.74 billion.
Internet content accounted for sales of $3.40 billion, Zona said.
"We see the content area growing substantially as more services enter the Internet space," Auditore said in a conference call with reporters.
